title: Choose the visual world for rqsystems.pt
question: Three directions for the full redesign. Pick one, steer, or re-roll. Copy stays as written in every direction.

options.label: Modernist Tile Wall
options.lineage: 1950s-60s Lisbon façade tiles and Maria Keil's Metro station panels
options.thesis: One module drawn once, then repeated across the whole wall without a hand touching it: that is what RQ builds.
options.viewport: Headline in wide Archivo across five tile units on the left; on the right, a Three.js relief-tile wall that starts with one uneven hand-painted tile and fills tile by tile with the clean pattern. Contact us is an ochre tile.
options.risk: Turns into a tourist souvenir if it drifts toward baroque blue-and-white; it has to stay geometric and modernist.

raised.raise: The headline is set at the scale of the wall: it spans tile units and carries the structure instead of captioning the art.
The page runs as ordered stations (find the manual work, draw the module, install it, iterate), each one a panel set into the wall.
The wall is generated from a seeded sequence, not a static image, so the pattern is real geometry that holds identically on every load.
The glaze highlight follows the pointer, so the visitor's attention is what lights the wall.
Each scroll step reveals one panel along a single axis; nothing competes for the eye.

options.label: The Archive Shelf
options.lineage: the Portuguese office archive: lever-arch dossiers, spine labels, violet-ink carimbos
options.thesis: Every SME owner has the shelf of binders that holds the manual work; RQ stamps it done.
options.viewport: A full-width shelf of 3D binders with the headline on the shelf's label strip. A violet stamp slams AUTOMATED across the spines one by one, then the binders slide back into the wall. Contact us is a pull-tab on the nearest spine.
options.risk: Office-paper skeuomorphism is a familiar move, and a busy shelf becomes clutter; it only works with few spines and big type.

options.label: Operations Guide Map
options.lineage: fold-out zoo and gardens guide maps
options.thesis: The business drawn as a guide map: each department is a lobe of land, the handoffs are the coastline, and automation lays the paths.
options.viewport: One green lobe swells off two edges of the frame with the headline set on it; a yellow Contact us capsule is pinned to the coastline like a gate marker.
options.case: Holds product clarity: discovery-first reads directly as mapping the operation. It loses on premium audience identification, because a leisure-map register can undersell a B2B agency.
options.risk: Reads playful or children's-map if the type is set loosely; it drops Three.js entirely.

options.label: Futurist Bolted Book
options.thesis: Every section a typographic collision at engine speed.
options.viewport: Angled wood-type shout across a bolted spread.
options.case: Fuses poorly: SME owners deciding whether to trust an agency get shouted at.
options.risk: Loud reads as unserious for a B2B buyer.
options.kept: Type at architectural scale doing structural work.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Work moves through fixed stations under amber light.
options.viewport: A print emerging in the developer tray.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither the audience nor the offer lives in a darkroom.
options.risk: Moody and slow where the visitor needs to act.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black-and-white data strobing as a barcode wall.
options.viewport: A frozen barcode field with a sine lattice.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it sits on the tech-agency rut and alienates non-technical owners.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Paths light up two steps ahead of the visitor.
options.case: Fuses poorly: near-black with neon glow is exactly the AI-startup look the brief refuses.

options.label: Versailles Vistas
options.thesis: Axial vistas opening into hidden bosquets.
options.viewport: A palace-terrace axis to the horizon.
options.case: Fuses poorly: royal grandeur contradicts two engineers talking to you directly.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean light agency site: white ground, near-black type, one accent and product screenshots, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Split hero: headline and buttons on the left, a product visual on the right.
canonCard.risk: Close to the current build and indistinguishable from other agencies by design.
